The market consensus signal bridges these by quantifying how much the collective betting behavior deviates from initial expectations. This structure enables GSI to model belief evolution through Bayesian inference, where each new odds update acts as a likelihood function. The GSE leverages this for state transitions, simulating how teams' performance might alter betting dynamics. Failure modes include stale data, which breaks the temporal coherence of the system, and reliance on non-keyless sources, violating operational constraints. Dualities emerge in the symmetry between pre-game and live states, and the duality of belief vs. evidence in the Bayesian framework.
